title: Come, Bless the Lord

questions.question: Come, bless the Lord, all you servants of the Lord, who stand by night in the house of whom?
questions.explanation: Psalm 134:1 (ESV): "...who stand by night in the house of the Lord!"

questions.question: Lift up your hands to the holy place and bless whom?
questions.explanation: Psalm 134:2 (ESV): "Lift up your hands to the holy place and bless the Lord!"

questions.question: May the Lord bless you from where?
questions.explanation: Psalm 134:3 (ESV): "May the Lord bless you from Zion,"

questions.question: He who made what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 134:3 (ESV): "he who made heaven and earth!"

questions.question: This is the last of the Songs of what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 134 is the final Song of Ascents (120-134).

questions.question: Who are addressed in verse 1?
questions.explanation: Psalm 134:1 (ESV): "...all you servants of the Lord,"

questions.question: When do these servants stand in the house of the Lord?
questions.explanation: Psalm 134:1 (ESV): "...who stand by night in the house of the Lord!"

questions.question: What posture of prayer is mentioned?
Who is usually identified as the "servants of the Lord" here?
questions.explanation: Those who ministered in the temple, especially at night.

questions.question: How many verses does Psalm 134 have?
The blessing in verse 3 is distinct because it changes from plural (you all) to what?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew grammar shifts to singular "you" (bless you), like a priestly blessing on the worshiper.

questions.question: This Psalm might have been used as a call and response between whom?
options: Worshipers leaving and the temple watch
questions.correctAnswer: Worshipers leaving and the temple watch
questions.explanation: A common interpretation: pilgrims bless the night watch, who bless them back.

questions.question: What characterizes the Lord in the final verse?
What word is repeated 3 times in 3 verses?
questions.explanation: Bless (barak) appears in all three verses.

key_verse_text: Come, bless the Lord, all you servants of the Lord, who stand by night in the house of the Lord!
